title: The last-coordinate product is the specified binary Kunneth comparison
statement:
Use the finite-coefficient purity conventions [def-pur-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, $n\geq1$, and $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. All schemes and morphisms below are separated finite type over $k$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Work with the small pro-etale derived categories, derived pullback and tensor [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], compact supports [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], Tate twists [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], and $D^b_{ctf}$ as in [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Write $\otimes=\otimes_A^L$ and $\rho$ for the right tensor unitor. Let $Y$ be such a scheme and $m\geq1$. Put $X_j=\mathbf A^j_Y$, $p=p_m:X_m\to Y$, $a=p_1:X_1\to Y$, and let $q:X_{m+1}\to X_m$ and $r:X_{m+1}\to X_1$ be the first-$m$ and last-coordinate projections [def-sbc-affine-space]. Thus $pq=ar=p_{m+1}$. Set $T_j=A_{X_j}(j)[2j]$, $T=T_1$, $V_j=Rp_{j!}T_j$, and $U=V_1$. Assume $V_m$, $U$ and $V_{m+1}$ are bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude. Use the concrete finite-coefficient exchanges and projection transformations of [def-exchange-projection], the normalized composition comparisons of [thm-sf-comp-composition], and the Tate pullback/tensor identifications fixed in [def-pur-affine-space-comparison], in particular
$$T_{m+1}=Lq^*T_m\otimes Lr^*T.$$
Let $\kappa_{m,1}:V_{m+1}\xrightarrow{\sim}V_m\otimes U$ be a supplied isomorphism equal to the specified binary relative compact-support product construction in [thm-sf-kunneth-relative] at $(p,T_m),(a,T)$; only that explicit construction is specified, and no abstract six-functor datum is assumed. Put
$$\alpha=\alpha_{p,q},\qquad E=\operatorname{Ex}_{!,a,p,T}:Lp^*U\xrightarrow{\sim}Rq_!Lr^*T,\qquad P_U=\operatorname{PF}_{p,T_m,U}.$$
Let
$$\Pi^q_{T_m}=\sigma_{Rq_!Lr^*T,T_m}\,\operatorname{PF}_{q,Lr^*T,T_m}^{-1}\,Rq_!(\sigma_{Lq^*T_m,Lr^*T})$$
be the two-symmetry inverse projection map, with $\sigma$ the signed tensor symmetry [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. The four projection transformations at $(q,Lr^*T,T_m)$, $(p,T_m,U)$, $(r,Lq^*T_m,T)$ and $(a,T,V_m)$, the exchanges for both product squares, and the relevant composition comparisons are invertible. Every tensor object appearing in the two forward-product composites of [lem-pur-finite-forward-product-symmetry] at $(p,T_m),(a,T)$ is bounded below and of etale origin. Under the indicated twist and tensor identifications, the actual morphisms satisfy
$$\kappa_{m,1}=P_U^{-1}\,Rp_!(1_{T_m}\otimes E^{-1})\,Rp_!(\Pi^q_{T_m})\,\alpha_{T_{m+1}}^{-1}.$$
This identifies two maps in the derived category; it neither evaluates an integration map nor asserts coordinate-permutation invariance of a purity comparison.

proof.text: Put $M=T_m$, $N=T$, $Q=Lq^*M$, $R=Lr^*N$, $H=Q\otimes R=T_{m+1}$ and $W=Rq_!R$. The schemes and maps are separated finite type by the hypotheses. The finite Tate sheaves $A_{X_m}(m)$ and $A_{X_1}(1)$ are locally constant rank-one sheaves by [prop-weil-twist-preserves]; since $A$ is finite they are constructible. Their shifts $M,N$ are bounded constructible, so [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin](ii) supplies bounded-below etale-origin witnesses. All further tensor-domain conditions for the two forward products are explicitly assumed in the item. Thus the forward-product symmetry applies to $(f,g;M,N)=(p,a;T_m,T)$; no abstract six-functor datum has been supplied or is needed.

source.place: Symmetry clause (i), applied to the binary product in sk-prop-an Step 6; explicit inversion of the supplied forward-product symmetry

proof.text:
Let $F=\Xi_{p,a}(M,N):V_m\otimes U\to Rp_{m+1!}H$ be the explicit forward map in [lem-pur-finite-forward-product-symmetry]. The assumption identifying $\kappa_{m,1}$ with the binary construction in [thm-sf-kunneth-relative] says precisely $F=\kappa_{m,1}^{-1}$: reversing the factors of that specified inverse construction gives
$$F=\alpha_{a,r}\,Ra_!(\operatorname{PF}_{r,Q,N})\,Ra_!(\operatorname{Ex}_{!,p,a,M}\otimes1_N)\,Ra_!(\sigma_{N,La^*V_m})\,\operatorname{PF}_{a,N,V_m}\,\sigma_{V_m,U}.$$
Every factor here is invertible by the hypotheses. This step only unfolds the construction stipulated in the item; it does not apply the relative-product theorem, whose general assertion assumes a six-functor datum.

source.place: Symmetry clause (i), applied to the binary product in sk-prop-an Step 6; explicit inversion of the supplied forward-product symmetry

proof.text:
For the swapped fibre product use the same scheme $X_{m+1}$ with the projections interchanged: it is a pullback of $(a,p)$ because the pullback universal property is unchanged by interchanging its two legs. Thus on this common model the swap identification is the identity on the underlying scheme, the swapped exterior product is $R\otimes Q$, and the map $S$ in [lem-pur-finite-forward-product-symmetry] is $Rp_{m+1!}(\sigma_{R,Q})$. Identity composition comparisons are normalized to identities by [thm-sf-comp-composition]. That symmetry theorem therefore gives
$$F=Rp_{m+1!}(\sigma_{R,Q})\,\Xi_{a,p}(N,M)\,\sigma_{V_m,U}.$$
Its hypotheses were checked in Step 1. This equality compares actual forward products; no integration map occurs.

source.place: Symmetry clause (i), applied to the binary product in sk-prop-an Step 6; explicit inversion of the supplied forward-product symmetry

proof.text:
Write $C=\operatorname{PF}_{q,R,M}$ and $P_U=\operatorname{PF}_{p,M,U}$. Expanding the swapped forward map by [lem-pur-finite-forward-product-symmetry] gives
$$\Xi_{a,p}(N,M)=\alpha_{p,q}\,Rp_!(C)\,Rp_!(E\otimes1_M)\,Rp_!(\sigma_{M,Lp^*U})\,P_U\,\sigma_{U,V_m}.$$
In Step 3 the last symmetry cancels $\sigma_{V_m,U}$. Naturality of $\alpha$ in [thm-sf-comp-composition] gives
$$Rp_{m+1!}(\sigma_{R,Q})\,\alpha_{p,q,R\otimes Q}=\alpha_{p,q,H}\,Rp_!Rq_!(\sigma_{R,Q}).$$
Naturality of the signed symmetry gives
$$(E\otimes1_M)\sigma_{M,Lp^*U}=\sigma_{M,W}(1_M\otimes E).$$
For completeness the symmetry identities used here are elementary: on homogeneous tensors the double swap multiplies by $(-1)^{ij+ji}=1$, and a degree-zero morphism in either factor commutes with $(-1)^{ij}$. These identities pass through the K-flat models defining the specified derived symmetry. Consequently, with
$$B=Rq_!(\sigma_{R,Q})\,C\,\sigma_{M,W}:M\otimes W\to Rq_!H,$$
we obtain $F=\alpha_{p,q,H}\,Rp_!(B)\,Rp_!(1_M\otimes E)\,P_U$.

source.place: Symmetry clause (i), applied to the binary product in sk-prop-an Step 6; explicit inversion of the supplied forward-product symmetry

proof.text:
By its definition in the item,
$$\Pi^q_{T_m}=\sigma_{W,M}\,C^{-1}\,Rq_!(\sigma_{Q,R}).$$
Compose this map with $B$ in either order. The adjacent symmetries cancel, $C^{-1}C$ or $CC^{-1}$ cancels, and the remaining adjacent symmetries cancel as well. Hence $B^{-1}=\Pi^q_{T_m}$. Tensor functoriality [lem-weil-derived-tensor-functorial] gives $(1_M\otimes E)^{-1}=1_M\otimes E^{-1}$; direct-image functors also carry inverse pairs to inverse pairs. Inverting the final composite in Step 4, and using $F^{-1}=\kappa_{m,1}$ from Step 2, proves
$$\kappa_{m,1}=P_U^{-1}\,Rp_!(1_M\otimes E^{-1})\,Rp_!(\Pi^q_{T_m})\,\alpha_{p,q,H}^{-1}.$$
This is the asserted equality after the already fixed identification $H=T_{m+1}$. All signed symmetries have been retained and cancelled in pairs; no purity comparison or coordinate-permutation invariance has been invoked.
